teams.heading: Steve Hansen says Mark Nawaqanitawase would be better off playing for Fiji
teams.body: Nawaqanitawase, 26, is still weighing his Test options after returning to 15s following two years in rugby league with the Sydney Roosters. He has signed with Japan's Saitama Wild Knights and is eligible for Italy and Fiji as well as Australia, for whom he has 11 caps. On the Rugby Unity podcast, Hansen said that if the wing prioritises Japan, he "would be better off playing for Fiji." Hansen also said Nawaqanitawase needs to decide reasonably quickly.

lead.why: The strongest new item in the pack, and it concerns a player who could become available to Fiji, while the other new item is only a schedule search result.

teams.heading: Lee Blackett names George Ford and Fin Smith as England's squad leaders
teams.body: England attack coach Lee Blackett has named George Ford and Fin Smith among the squad's leaders as camp gets under way for Australia. The newcomers come from nine different clubs and run different shapes and lines, so the coaches want everyone "on the same page". Ford, Blackett says, is "a dream to work with as a 10", while Henry Slade has settled back in comfortably. The Australia test is just over a week away.

lead.why: A new, England-specific squad story from the camp, naming the players Blackett sees leading the group ahead of Australia.

teams.heading: Galthié loses injured Brau-Boirie, Hastoy and Gazzotti, calls up Jelonch and Depoortere
teams.body: Fabien Galthié has been forced into late changes to his extended squad after Brau-Boirie, Hastoy and Gazzotti all picked up injuries in Top 14 action and will miss the resumption of the competition. Planet Rugby also lists Karl Sorin among the withdrawals. Nicolas Depoortere, Anthony Jelonch and the uncapped Louis Le Brun are called in, with Thomas Laclayat also added. The November block now runs against Fiji, the Springboks and Argentina, with Jalibert, Ramos and Marchand already absent.

lead.why: It is the freshest France men's XV story in the pack, with late squad withdrawals and replacements for the November Tests.

teams.heading: Gus McCarthy to captain Ireland XV against Fiji A, Edogbo brothers included
teams.body: Ireland XV head coach Mark Sexton has named a 28-man squad for next month's game against Fiji A in Cork, with Leinster hooker Gus McCarthy captaining the side. Sexton's squad includes Edwin and Seán Edogbo, both Munster forwards, and Kieran Brookes, who last wore an Ireland jersey as a teenager before going on to play Test rugby for England. Sexton called it "a meaningful fixture against what is a talented Fiji side."

teams.heading: Quesada says 17 Italy players are unavailable as captaincy call looms
teams.body: Gonzalo Quesada says 17 players are unavailable for Italy's autumn Tests, a significant difficulty given they are key figures. Four consecutive matches against top-ten opponents, starting with South Africa in Turin, are among the most demanding in Italy's history, he says. He will decide on the captaincy next week, with Giacomo Nicotera and Niccolò Cannone, both former captains, among the options. Tommaso Allan is under consideration for the 23 but has not yet trained fully, with full training targeted the following week.

lead.why: It is the newest item, and it puts a specific injury count and a pending captaincy decision on the table ahead of the autumn Tests.

teams.heading: Duhan van der Merwe released from Scotland squad to play for Edinburgh
teams.body: Duhan van der Merwe has been released from Scotland's squad to return to Edinburgh for their United Rugby Championship match against Benetton, with Gregor Townsend wanting the winger to build match fitness. It is not a punishment, and he remains part of the 37-man squad for November. He has played just 18 minutes this season, a comeback against the Lions cut short by a dislocated finger. Townsend said: "It was a much better outcome than it looked at the time."

teams.heading: Macs Page called into Wales squad after Rio Dyer hamstring withdrawal
teams.body: Wales have made a late change to their squad for the November Nations Championship, with Dragons wing Rio Dyer released after a hamstring injury suffered in the 31-14 defeat to Ospreys last Saturday. Dyer had only just been recalled. Steve Tandy has called up uncapped Scarlets back Macs Page in his place, Page's first senior call-up since July. He becomes the fourth uncapped player in the extended squad, alongside Rhys Barratt, Che Hope and Aneurin Owen.

teams.heading: Thomas Gallo sidelined for at least six months after wrist surgery in Lyon
teams.body: Thomas Gallo, Argentina's prop, will be sidelined for at least six months after dislocating his left wrist in Lyon's 31-27 win at Bayonne, with an operation on Saturday. Rodrigo Martínez of the Dragons has replaced him in Felipe Contepomi's 33-man squad, which began a three-day mini-camp in London on Monday ahead of the Ireland opener. The loss removes a loosehead option at the start of a three-test European tour.

lead.why: A loosehead prop out for at least six months is the most concrete squad story in the pack, and it is not in the already-reported list.

teams.heading: Fraser McReight wins maiden John Eales Medal as Rob Valetini misses out
teams.body: Fraser McReight has claimed his maiden John Eales Medal at the Rugby Australia Awards in Sydney, beating Jeremy Williams and Rob Valetini, who was denied a third-straight medal. He also won Defender of the Year for Wallabies vs France in Brisbane earlier in the night. The Reds superstar joins the likes of Michael Hooper, David Pocock and George Smith among legendary opensides to claim the award.

teams.heading: NZ Rugby's Steve Lancaster opens door to relaxing All Blacks selection policy
teams.body: New Zealand Rugby could relax its strict policy on picking All Blacks who do not play for one of the five Super Rugby Pacific clubs, Planet Rugby reports. The union on Thursday backed Super Rugby Pacific and the NPC as the right competitions for the All Blacks, keeping the status quo over a proposal to replace Super Rugby Pacific with an 8-10 team national competition. NZR chief Steve Lancaster's comments hint at a policy shift, with the final Board decision still to come and implementation expected from 2028.

lead.why: It is the highest-scoring new item and concerns the All Blacks' own selection policy, which matters beyond this November tour.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus names six uncapped players in Springboks November squad
teams.body: Erasmus has named six uncapped players in his squad for the November Nations Championship matches, with Handré Pollard missing through injury. Yaqeen Ahmed and Luan Giliomee are the fly-half options, to compete with settled pair Feinberg-Mngomezulu and Manie Libbok. Four players who featured for the Junior Boks this year are included, among them lock Riley Norton and centre Markus Muller. South Africa face Italy, France and Ireland before the finals weekend.
